question: In ESOI, intents are meaningful containers of a set of specifications. For human understanding, they serve as a personal category of interest or relate to a tangible container such as an organization.
What is a specific phrase which distinguishes the topic of the intent from other intents?
What is this intent manifesting in present tense? e.g. "I am ..." or "The world is ..." Any subject and verb can be used.
What are potentials inspired by this intent?

A general category like "parenting" or "career." An intent is also not an organization itself, rather the container of specification that clarifies why the organization exists (as a solution and implementation within an intent). In this example, different versions of the same organization can be documented as separate alternative implementations.
A description of what motivated the intent. A challenge, difficulty, or description of how an ideal is not reached.

What are the solution's priorities in order? Each milestone is a value of one or more metrics, which doesn't have to be the authoritative metric directly but it should relate to it. End condition (optional): Condition for the milestone to no longer be a priority (date or other circumstance), at which point it's archived. Target completion time (optional): Planned completion date and time (which other dependent milestones may rely on). May be a date or a specific minute of a date where precision is needed.
What knowledge informs the solution's definition or implementations?
What would indicate the solution is successful?

What classifications may be necessary to avoid risk? Possible risks (structural problems): R1: Adding a new solution that duplicates an existing one. R2: Not leveraging the benefits of an existing solution, such as partial overlap of purpose. R3: Not being aware of solutions that need to change definition or implementation due to something else changing. R4: Using a solution when it should not be for the particular use case.

Every tag should name what risk it mitigates, which are linked problems, whether from the same intent as the solution or from other intents (such as R1-R4 above which are problems defined for ESOI). Consequently, a solution's connected problems are also tags but are not sufficient on their own.

A practical way to measure the distance between the implementations of a solution and an ideal which the solution was defined to achieve. Alternative implementations are compared via metrics. Consequently, every solution has only one authoritative metric, which can be a combination of multiple metrics or factors with weights that reflect the solution's ideals and purpose. Note: Metrics can also be solutions, as metrics themselves may be refined over time with alternative implementations (including dataset versions).
